stem: Let $f(\theta) = a\cos\theta + q$, where $a = {=a}$ and $q = {=q}$. The graph of $f$ is drawn for $0^\circ \leq \theta \leq 360^\circ$. Which of the following is the range of $f$?
solution: For $y = \cos\theta$ the highest value is $1$ and the lowest value is $-1$.
Multiplying by $a = {=a}$ stretches the graph, so the amplitude is $|a| = {=a}$ and $a\cos\theta$ runs from ${=0 - a}$ up to ${=a}$.
Adding $q = {=q}$ moves every point of the graph up by $q$ units (down if $q$ is negative), so the lowest value is $q - a = {=q - a}$ and the highest value is $q + a = {=q + a}$.
The range is ${=q - a} \leq f(\theta) \leq {=q + a}$.

proposed_misconceptions.label: Forgets the vertical shift q when stating the range
proposed_misconceptions.description: Gives the range of a cos θ, from -a to a, without moving it up or down by q.

proposed_misconceptions.label: Forgets the amplitude a when stating the range
proposed_misconceptions.description: Shifts the range of cos θ, from -1 to 1, by q but does not stretch it by the factor a.

proposed_misconceptions.label: Moves the range the wrong way for q
proposed_misconceptions.description: Subtracts q from both ends of the range of a cos θ, so a positive q moves the graph down and a negative q moves it up.

notes: The book items of this objective read the amplitude off a drawn graph (two of them, 6-19c and 6-20c, have q not zero and a negative); no figure can be sampled, so the family asks for the range of a given f(θ) = a cos θ + q on 0 to 360 degrees. Range is written as an inequality, not interval notation, so no bracket or separator convention can mismatch. a is positive here (the reflected case is in the advanced families); q is never 0 and a is at least 2, so the four options are always different (D1 equals the correct option only if q = 0, D2 only if a = 1, D3 only if q = 0). The engine's range convention is the book's: lowest value q - |a|, highest value q + |a|.
